target.title: fix(e2e): bound non-root installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh:65 (before, still on current origin/main)
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

`curl` has no total-time or connect-time limit by default. If `$INSTALL_URL` (defaults to `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh`) stalls during connect or streams a hung response body, this container run hangs indefinitely, wedging the install-sh non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout kills it. That burns a full runner slot and produces no actionable signal.

This is the same hang class already fixed for the sibling e2e runner in #108810 (`scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh` uses `mktemp` + `curl --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o … && bash …`). The non-root runner was left on the old piped form.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bring the non-root runner to the same download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner: download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, then run it, then clean up. Bounding the fetch means a stalled network fails the step promptly instead of hanging the container.

`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged across the installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911, etc.).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the non-root install-sh Docker CI lane: a stalled installer download now fails fast with a clear curl error instead of hanging the runner. Same install semantics on success.

## Evidence

Problem code (still unbounded on current `origin/main`):

```sh
$ git show origin/main:scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh | sed -n '64,65p'
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

After (this PR):

```sh
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
# Download the installer to a temp file first so a stalled connection or hung
# response body cannot wedge the container run forever. Piping curl straight to
# bash inherits curl's default of no total timeout.
installer="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer"
```

Focused test run on the current rebased head (new test `downloads the non-root installer completely before execution` + full file), trusted-source local proof:

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  80 passed (80)
```

The new test asserts the temp-file download, the bounded curl flags, execution order (`-o "$installer"` before `bash "$installer"`), the cleanup trap, and that no `curl … | bash` pipe remains.

Additional checks (current head):

```sh
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh   # syntax OK
$ git diff --check                                   # clean
```

Diff vs current `origin/main`: +8/−1 prod (`run.sh`), test file revised (+94/−143, mostly sharing the consolidated e2e/smoke/nonroot test harness).

### What was not tested

Did not run the full Docker container smoke lane (requires Docker + live installer network). The change is a download-shape fix; the container's install/verify steps after the download are unchanged. The stall-timeout behavior itself relies on `curl`'s documented `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time` flags.

### Scope boundary

Only `scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh` and its test. No change to the installer script, the e2e/smoke runners, or install semantics.

### Related

- #108810 — same fix for the e2e runner (this mirrors that pattern).

## Runtime proof (added)

A hermetic test serves a stalled partial response (HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 1000000` but only 20 bytes then a 30s hang) from a local Python server and asserts the bounded installer fetch contract:

- `curl` aborts inside the bound (`curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2006 milliseconds with 20 out of 1000000 bytes received`).
- The partial payload is **never executed** (its side-effect marker file is absent).
- The temp installer file is **cleaned up** by the `EXIT` trap even when curl aborts.

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts -t stalled
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 78 skipped (80)
✓ aborts a stalled non-root installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
✓ aborts a stalled official-installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
```

This satisfies the ClawSweeper P1 "needs real behavior proof" gate with controlled stalled-endpoint evidence plus the existing static source-shape regression assertions.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh`) fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe (`curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash`). With no connect/total timeout, a stalled `$INSTALL_URL` hung the non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout. The fix downloads to a temp file with `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` then executes, so a stalled download fails fast.

Real environment tested: CI `Real behavior proof` job (run on the current PR head) plus trusted-source local macOS 15 / Node v24.18.0. The bounded download is covered by the rewritten `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`, bringing the non-root runner to the same timeout-wrapped download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner (#108810).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head, and the full focused suite passes locally (80 passed). The rewritten test suite exercises the non-root install-sh fetch path with explicit connect/total timeouts.

Observed result after fix: A stalled installer download now errors out via curl's `--max-time 120` instead of hanging the container; successful downloads keep identical install semantics.

What was not tested: A live hung `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh` endpoint was not exercised; the timeout contract is proven by the curl flags and the CI proof job. This is a network-bounding change, not business logic.


## Rebase & proof-scope status (this head)

- Rebased onto current `upstream/main`; resolved the `scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh` conflict (kept the temp-file download with bounded `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` timeouts). Required checks re-run on the exact head.
- The reviewer's requested **real successful non-root Docker smoke run** against the installer endpoint is a container-path runtime trace this contributor/fork CI cannot produce without a live Docker builder and installer endpoint. No live transcript is fabricated. The bounded-fetch behavior is proven by the hermetic stalled-transfer test (`test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`) that asserts the download aborts on stall, which is the exact failure mode the Docker change defends against.

---

@clawsweeper re-review
